facts.text: The fan-tailed cuckoo is found in Australia, Fiji, New Caledonia, New Guinea, Solomon Islands, and Vanuatu.
facts.quote: It is found in Australia, Fiji, New Caledonia, New Guinea, Solomon Islands, and Vanuatu.

facts.text: The fan-tailed cuckoo has a slate-grey head, back and wings, rufous underparts and a barred black and white tail.
facts.quote: The fan-tailed cuckoo has a slate-grey head, back and wings, rufous underparts and barred black and white tail.

facts.text: A yellow orbital eye ring helps to distinguish the fan-tailed cuckoo from the smaller and paler brush cuckoo.
facts.quote: Its eye is surrounded by a yellow orbital eye ring which helps to distinguish it from the smaller and paler brush cuckoo (C. variolosus) and the also smaller chestnut-breasted cuckoo (C. castaneiventris).

facts.text: The fan-tailed cuckoo eats insects, fruits, vegetables, small reptiles, mammals and birds, especially bird chicks.
facts.quote: The species in Australia eats a variety of insect and their larvae, fruits and vegetables, small reptiles, mammals and birds, especially bird chicks.

facts.text: It perches in an exposed position to locate its prey and then pounces, catching it in the air or on the ground.
facts.quote: It perches in an exposed position to locate its prey and then pounces, catching it in the air or on the ground.

facts.text: In Australia the fan-tailed cuckoo breeds from July to January.
facts.quote: In Australia the species breeds from July to January.

facts.text: It lays only one mauve white egg, spotted with red and/or brown, in the nests of other birds like fairywrens or thornbills.
facts.quote: They only lay one mauve white with red and/or brown spotted egg in the nest of other birds (see brood parasitism) like fairywrens or thornbills.

facts.text: Its voice is a descending trill with a grasshopper-like chirp.
facts.quote: Its voice is similar to descending trill with a grasshopper-like chirp.

facts.text: It lives in temperate forests, mangrove forests, montane forests, paddocks, orchards and gardens.
facts.quote: Its natural habitats are temperate forests, subtropical or tropical mangrove forests, subtropical or tropical moist montane forests, paddocks, orchards and gardens.
